t: You're looking at a bronze statue of George Peabody, tucked behind the Royal Exchange in the City of London. Peabody was an American businessman and philanthropist, and he's honoured here for his giving to housing in London. He set up the Peabody Donation Fund, one of the country's largest housing associations, to offer affordable homes to working-class citizens. Over his lifetime he gave away the equivalent of eighty-seven million pounds, and he's often called the father of modern philanthropy. The statue was made by the American sculptor William Wetmore Story.
